- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent sentiment is positive and forecast peaks sharply after a spike, cap the overshoot at +5% above recent 7-day average.  
- If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast in early days of 30d horizon, apply a 3–5% downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated small positive swings, expect mean reversion within 5–7 days — adjust forecast to align with recent 10-day moving average.  
- If forecast is >10% above recent 14-day high and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, reduce forecast by 10–15% to avoid overestimating bullish momentum.
